# Engineering calculations (analytical, ESTIMATED)

> Closed-form first-order sizing. Inputs marked **A** in `mechanical/design_params.yaml` are assumptions. Nothing here is a measurement, and no finite-element analysis has been run. Formulas are in `mechanical/harvestx_mech/calcs.py` with unit tests.

Tool + payload mass used: **2.17 kg** (end-effector mass from the CAD model + maximum head mass).

## 1. Cutting force and blade actuator

Upper bound for a straight chop: F = tau x pi d^2 / 4 with tau = 0.35 MPa (**assumed placeholder**) and d = 20 mm gives **110 N**. No reduction is credited for the slicing action, although published work on lettuce stems reports large reductions with a sliding cut.

- Actuator torque at 42 mm radius with safety factor 2: **9.2 N·m**
- Blade in-plane bending stress 57 MPa, factor of safety on yield 3.8 (annealed 304; a hardened blade steel is stronger). Lateral buckling and edge loading are not analysed.
- The blade closes against the fork edge, so the cutting force is internal to the end effector and is not transmitted to the gantry.

## 2. Fork tines carrying the cut head

- Load per tine (2x dynamic factor): 3.9 N at the tip
- Bending stress 6 MPa, factor of safety 38.1; tip deflection 0.06 mm

## 2b. Flat boom (weak-axis bending)

- Load 23.4 N (cut head + fork head, 2x dynamic) at the boom end: stress 34 MPa, factor of safety 6.4; free-air tip sag **2.1 mm** when lifted clear of the channel

## 3. Tool-point lateral stiffness

Z ram (350 mm overhang) plus shank (300 mm) as a stepped cantilever under 10 N lateral contact force (assumed):

- Bending 0.16 mm + torsion of the tubes acting over the boom offset 0.26 mm = **0.42 mm** at the stem seat (stiffness 23.9 N/mm); joint and guide compliance are not included, so the real value will be larger. This is small against the 25 mm capture half-width, and the fork is located vertically by the channel, not by the ram.
- Ram root stress 1.3 MPa, factor of safety 216

## 4. Y bridge

- Central load 149 N on a 1220 mm span: deflection 0.146 mm, stress 3.2 MPa, factor of safety 85
- Section is a hollow-rectangle idealisation; replace with the extrusion manufacturer's section properties when the profile is selected.

## 5. Axis drive requirements

Torque includes safety factor 2.

| axis | drive | carried mass [kg] | thrust [N] | motor torque [N·m] | speed [rpm] | peak power [W] | gravity holding torque [N·m] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| X | belt | 37.2 | 82 | 2.72 | 318 | 41 | 0.000 |
| Y | belt | 15.2 | 33 | 1.11 | 318 | 17 | 0.000 |
| Z | screw | 6.2 | 70 | 0.26 | 1500 | 17 | 0.096 |

Sum of peak mechanical power 75 W (axes never peak together; electrical sizing in Phase 4 adds driver efficiency, logic, lighting and compute). The Z axis needs a brake or a self-locking drive: gravity holding torque is non-zero.

## 6. Tool-flange bolts (4 x M6 on 50 mm pitch circle)

- Moment 7.3 N·m, max bolt tension 156 N, factor of safety on A2-70 proof load **58** (preload and fatigue not analysed)

## 7. Stem capture by the V-throat

Usable half-width (entry half-width minus stem radius): 25 mm. Probability that the lateral error is inside it, using the 1-sigma errors from the **synthetic** perception benchmark:

| target source | sigma [mm] | P(captured) |
|---|---|---|
| fixture prior only | 6.5 | 0.99988 |
| RGB-D + fixture fusion | 6.1 | 0.99996 |
| RGB-D vision only | 15.4 | 0.8955 |

Gaussian tails are optimistic; gross errors (wrong plant, leaning stem outside the net pot) are not covered and are the reason for the stem-seated sensor.

| descend in the plant-free flank (z) | 1.37 |
| flank traverse towards the channel (y) | 0.75 |

About 329 plants per hour for one tool on one rack section, **estimated** from kinematic limits only. Not a throughput claim.
